subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and must the cache be per-reviewer-instance with the full reviewed input as its key?
rationale: The source-level cost bug is clear, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes when a later request bypasses a fresh model review, so the approval-boundary intent cannot be chosen by cleanup automation alone.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

options.title: Cache allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once decisions and keep ask, timeout, and error outcomes uncached for a narrower security-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept the repeated reviewer completion cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger live billing or security evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent approval-reviewer security work makes this the best available route for the cache-boundary decision.
